info.title: Platform 5E API
info.description:
Backend of **Platform 5E**: teachers upload the material of a unit, generate 5E learning resources that cite it
(RAG), review them and export the approved ones to Moodle (Moodle XML) or Chamilo (SCORM 1.2).

**Authentication.** `POST /api/v1/accounts` or `POST /api/v1/sessions` return a bearer token. Click *Authorize* and
paste only the token. Private routes answer 401 without it.

**Errors.** Every error has the same shape: `{"error": {"code": "UNIT_NOT_FOUND", "message": "…"}}`. The `code` is
stable and in English; the `message` is shown to the teacher, so it is in Spanish.

**Stored values.** Review statuses (`pendiente`, `aprobado`, `descartado`), resource types (`item_opcion_multiple`…)
and difficulties (`basica`, `intermedia`, `avanzada`) are values saved in the database. They move to English in
Sprint 2 together with a data migration.

post.description:
Validates the unit ownership, the outcome and that the unit has processed material, saves the request
and runs it in the background (202 with `Location`). Poll `GET /generation-requests/{requestId}` for the
status of each step.

The client sends a stable `Idempotency-Key`, unique per teacher. Repeating the same key with the same body
(mode, unit and parameters) returns the existing request (200) without applying the other rules again;
using it with a different body returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Without processed material the request
is rejected (400 NO_PROCESSED_MATERIAL), and a teacher with 2 active requests gets 429 with `Retry-After`.

Example (Bash/cURL). Set BASE_URL to the API URL and TOKEN to a valid bearer token.
Use your own ids for path variables and replace sample ids such as unidad-1 in JSON bodies.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -i -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v1/generation-requests" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"mode":"sequence","unitId":"unidad-1","resourceTypes":["pregunta_detonante","item_opcion_multiple"],"quantity":1}'
```

Replace unidad-1 with a unit containing processed material. Expected 202; repeat with the same key to get 200.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Stable client key, unique per teacher: 8 to 128 letters, digits, `-` or `_`. Reuse it when retrying the same request. Without it the API answers 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED; with another format, 422 INVALID_PARAMETERS.

post.summary: Generate resources from the unit material (deprecated)
post.description:
Deprecated: use `POST /generation-requests`, which runs in the background with an idempotency key. This
synchronous route keeps working the same until the evaluation scripts migrate, and is then removed.

Retrieves the most relevant chunks of the unit (BM25) and drafts the resources with the active generator.

Only resources whose claims cite valid chunks are kept; they are saved as `pendiente` for the teacher's review.
If the AI fails, the rule-based generator answers and `generator.fallback` is true. Without material the
request is rejected (400 NO_PROCESSED_MATERIAL) instead of inventing content.

With `resourceTypes`, the request becomes a class sequence (HU-003): each type goes to the agent of its 5E
stage, in the order of the class; all agents share the same evidence and see what the previous ones wrote.
A resource too similar to another one of the sequence is asked again once and, if it still repeats, rejected.
Each resource records its `agent`, and `sequence` reports what every agent generated or rejected.

Example (Bash/cURL). Set BASE_URL to the API URL and TOKEN to a valid bearer token.
Use your own ids for path variables and replace sample ids such as unidad-1 in JSON bodies.

```bash

```

Replace unidad-1 with a unit containing processed material. Expected 200; returned resources await review.

put.summary: Save the review of a resource
put.description:
Saves edits and decisions. `aprobado` needs a key, no pending distractors and at least two accepted
(409 APPROVAL_BLOCKED otherwise): the same rule the review screen shows.

Send `expectedVersion` with the `version` you read. If the resource changed meanwhile (another tab), the save
is rejected with 409 VERSION_CONFLICT and nothing changes: reload the resource. When the verifiable content
changes, it is checked again against the stored evidence copy, without external services, and the result
comes in `verification`. An approved resource whose content changed goes back to `pendiente`
(`reviewReset: true`) and needs a new approval.

Example (Bash/cURL). Set BASE_URL to the API URL and TOKEN to a valid bearer token.
Use your own ids for path variables and replace sample ids such as unidad-1 in JSON bodies.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -i -X PUT "$BASE_URL/api/v1/units/${UNIT_ID}/resources/${RESOURCE_ID}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"expectedVersion":1,"title":"Glosario de transporte","body":"TCP confirma la recepción de datos.","status":"pendiente","edited":true}'
```

Use a resource in your unit; copy its actual title, content and version before saving. This example saves an edit as pendiente, not an approval. Expected 200.

post.summary: Retry the verification of a pending resource
post.description:
«Reintentar comprobación» (REV-C3): checks the same version again with the current rule and the stored
`evidenceThreshold`, using only the evidence copy saved in the resource (no external services). The version
does not change.

Only for `verification.status = pending` (409 VERIFICATION_NOT_PENDING). Without an evidence copy, or with a
referenced chunk missing from it, the retry is not offered: regenerate the resource (409 REGENERATION_REQUIRED).
An outdated `expectedVersion` returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT.


Use a resource whose verification is pending and send its current version. Expected 200.

get.summary: List the downloads of a unit
get.description:
The last 50 downloads, newest first.

Example (Bash/cURL). Set BASE_URL to the API URL and TOKEN to a valid bearer token.
Use your own ids for path variables and replace sample ids such as unidad-1 in JSON bodies.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -i -X GET "$BASE_URL/api/v1/units/${UNIT_ID}/downloads" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

Expected 200. See the response schema below for the returned fields.

post.summary: Export the approved resources of a unit
post.description:
Builds the file in the backend from the approved resources (fixed templates, never written by the AI),
records the download in the unit history and returns the file.

- `scorm_zip`: SCORM 1.2 package for Chamilo, one page per resource in 5E order; questions are graded.
- `moodle_xml`: Moodle question bank with the multiple-choice items.
- `documento`: printable HTML document of the approved unit resources, with evidence.

Example (Bash/cURL). Set BASE_URL to the API URL and TOKEN to a valid bearer token.
Use your own ids for path variables and replace sample ids such as unidad-1 in JSON bodies.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v1/units/${UNIT_ID}/exports" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"format":"scorm_zip","resourceIds":[]}' -D respuesta-headers.txt --output unidad-scorm.zip
```

Expected 200 when the unit has approved resources. An empty resourceIds selects every approved resource compatible with scorm_zip.
